description: Sort contract fixtures (Paket 9), JS only (Sort has no Rust implementation), run by tests/unit/sort-contract.test.ts against the real sortText (src/utils/sortLines.ts). Phase B wrote the target by hand and documented the old behaviour; Phase C1 implemented it, so every 'expected' is now asserted directly (the old outputs are in docs/analyse/Paket9-PhaseB-Sortiervertrag.md). Every case states all options explicitly. 'basis': 'decision' = product decision (Phase B review, OD decisions of Phase C1), 'derived' = follows from the rules. 'rules' refer to the contract below, 'finding' (F1-F9, D1, D6) to the Phase A report, 'resolved' to the open decision of Phase B that the case settles. 'icuNumeric': the expected order equals a stable sort with Intl.Collator('de', { numeric: true }) (plus R1), checked as fixture consistency. 'invalidMethods' expect { error: 'invalidMode' } (ProcessingError invalidInput / errors.invalidMode). 'properties' are corpora of equivalence classes in sort order: any input order must give the classes in this order, each class in input order. 'random' has no golden order: it is checked with a seeded random source and a chi-square test.

rules.R1: Empty and whitespace-only lines are data lines: they are kept and placed after all other lines, in input order, for ascending and descending order and every method, the random shuffle included (OD-7 B). Whitespace = the Unicode White_Space set of Paket 8 (src/utils/diff/whitespace.ts, isBlankLine): U+0085 is whitespace, U+FEFF and U+200B are not.
rules.R2: Alphabetical order is ICU collation with the explicit locale 'de' (never the host locale); whitespace and punctuation are not ignored, digits are characters (no numeric collation).
rules.R3: caseSensitive false: case is ignored, accents stay relevant (sensitivity 'accent'). caseSensitive true: case is an additional tertiary criterion of the collation (sensitivity 'variant'; for 'de' lowercase sorts before uppercase).
rules.R4: Lines with equal sort keys keep their input order (stable sort).
rules.R5: Reverse methods reverse the comparison, not the finished array: equal keys keep their input order, blank lines stay at the end.
rules.R6: Line length counts Unicode code points, not UTF-16 code units (a lone surrogate counts as one).
rules.R7: No implicit trim: leading and trailing whitespace is part of the sort key and of the output.
rules.R8: An unknown sort method (also an empty, differently cased or non-string value) is a controlled input error { error: 'invalidMode' }, never a silent default.
rules.R9: Line model of Paket 6: LF, CRLF, CR; the result uses the most frequent line ending of the input (tie: the first one) and keeps the trailing newline. Exception (OD-8 B): if the last result line is empty and the input has no trailing newline, a trailing newline is added, otherwise the empty line could not be told apart from a trailing newline and would be lost.
rules.N1: Natural: the same collation as alphabetical (R2, R3) with runs of ASCII digits compared by their numeric value: a number sorts where a digit sorts (after whitespace and punctuation, before letters), any length without precision loss. Levels like the collation: 1. base letters and numbers, 2. accents, 3. case (caseSensitive only), so a later number difference outweighs an earlier case or accent difference, exactly as in alphabetical.
rules.N2: Natural: an ASCII '-' is a sign when it stands at the line start or directly after whitespace and is directly followed by a digit. After letters, digits or punctuation it is text ('Datei-2', '2020-12-01', 'x(-5)'; OD-1 A, OD-2 A). '+' and U+2212 are text (OD-3 A).
rules.N3: Natural: the point is the decimal separator for a number that starts at the line start or after whitespace (with or without sign) and has exactly one point between two digit runs: 'Kapitel 1.10' < 'Kapitel 1.2', 'Preis 1.125' < 'Preis 1.25' (OD-4 B). Not at such a boundary ('v1.10') or with a second point followed by a digit ('1.2.10', OD-5 A), the point is text and every digit run is its own number. A decimal needs digits on both sides. The comma is never a decimal separator.
rules.N4: Natural: a number directly after a letter is a part of a label: 'v1.2' sorts before 'v1.10' (the point separates parts).
rules.N5: Natural: no special interpretation of dates, hexadecimal numbers or scientific notation; such text is compared by N1 to N4 only.
rules.N6: Natural: numerically equal spellings ('1', '01', '1.0', '1.00'; '-0', '0', '00') are ordered by the collation of the whole line after all other levels (OD-6 B): deterministic, independent of the input order. -0 equals 0 numerically.

random.note: Six permutations, chi-square with 5 degrees of freedom; 20.515 is the 0.999 quantile. sortText takes { random } (seeded mulberry32 in the tests), so the run is reproducible. Phase B: the old sort(() => Math.random() - 0.5) had chi-square 3616 (F3); Phase C1 (Fisher-Yates) must stay below the critical value. 'blankLinesInput': blank lines stay at the end in input order (R1, OD-7 B), the other lines are shuffled.
